STL stores coordinates but no units. The bounding box is shown as millimetres, which is what most slicers assume. If the numbers look exactly 25.4× too small, the model was probably authored in inches — open theScale Inspector to check it.

How to open an STL file without installing anything

  1. 1

    Drop the file onto the panel — or choose it from your disk

    Binary and ASCII STL both work. A 20 mm demo cube is built in if you just want to see the controls.

  2. 2

    Orbit, zoom, and inspect the mesh

    Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, shift-drag or right-drag to pan. Double-click resets the camera. Keyboard: arrow keys orbit, + and − zoom, 0 resets. Wireframe view makes individual triangles visible.

  3. 3

    Read the real dimensions before you slice

    The stats panel reports triangle count, format, file size, and the X × Y × Z bounding box. If the size is wrong, fix the scale before the print, not after.

Privacy proof, not a promise

Open your browser's Network tab, then load a file. You will see no request carrying the model. This page has no upload endpoint and no server-side parser to send it to — the STL stream is read by FileReaderand parsed into WebGL buffers in your tab. The same is true of the converterand the printability checker.

STL viewer questions

Short answers about formats, units, privacy, and file size.

Does this STL viewer upload my file?

No. The file is read with the browser's local FileReader API, parsed in memory, and rendered with WebGL. There is no upload endpoint on this page. If you open your browser's Network tab and load a model, you will not see the STL bytes leave your machine.

Can it open both binary and ASCII STL files?

Yes. The viewer checks the 84-byte binary header and the declared triangle count first, then falls back to ASCII vertex parsing. Both formats render the same way, and the stats panel tells you which one you opened.

Why does my model look tiny or enormous?

STL files are unitless. Most slicers assume millimetres, so a model authored in inches arrives 25.4 times too small. Check the bounding box in the stats panel and use the STL Scale Inspector to convert a target height into an exact slicer percentage.

Is there a file size limit?

There is no artificial upload limit, because nothing is uploaded. The practical limit is your device's memory and GPU. Very large meshes may take a few seconds to parse and can be slower to orbit on older hardware.

Does the viewer work offline?

The viewer logic runs locally and the file never needs a connection. After the first page load, the 3D preview and parsing continue to work offline. Web fonts or icon files that were not cached may fall back to system fonts while you are disconnected.

Can the viewer tell me if a model will print?

No. A viewer shows shape, not printability. Use the STL Printability Checker to test for open edges, non-manifold geometry, degenerate triangles, and inconsistent winding before you slice.
